title: Unbounded evaluation and coefficient comparison before descent
statement: Fix an ordinary strict-system image package S and normalized derived evaluation-extension packages PY and PX as in [def-pur-coefficient-system-image-data]. There exist normalized exact inverse images and total right-derived direct images on the system and level categories, with their K-injective computation and strict-map transpose formulas, and canonical evaluation, ordinary tensor, derived tensor, scalar-restriction and transition comparisons, including all representative, unit, counit and adjunction-mate equations. This is precisely the seventeen construction projections of CoefficientSystemDerivedImage, before joint conservativity, lower-bound preservation and the essential-image/normalization descent criterion. It asserts the unbounded comparison for all derived objects, independently of a bounded-below full-faithfulness hypothesis.

source.place: Zheng Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10, equation (4.10.1), via the derived left-extension Hom chain; original comparison proof steps 1–8.

proof.text: Transfer Grothendieck abelianness along the explicit strict coefficient-system equivalence, and use coefficient-universe Grothendieck abelianness at every level. K-injective resolutions give the right derivability structure. Mathlib localizes the exact inverse image and constructs total right-derived direct image; Adjunction.derived supplies the derived adjunction. Its derived unit formula and naturality give the required representative transpose normalization.

Use the fully faithful precomposition functor for localization to lift the ordinary inverse-evaluation and restriction-inverse-image squares, with their explicit representative equations. The ordinary restriction square has invertible right mate: apply the faithful underlying-sheaf functor and the ordinary transpose normalization. The evaluation square has the prescribed right-evaluation mate by the system transpose formula. The four-adjunction mates correspondence therefore gives the ordinary tensor and ordinary extension comparisons, normalized on units.

Construct a common adapted resolution for each exact inverse-image functor. The free sheaf adjunction identifies inverse image of a free module with the free module on the inverse-image sheaf. Thus free terms are flat on both sides. Resolve in the retract-stable subcategory of modules flat before and after inverse image using the reduced free left resolution. Its filtered colimit of bounded-above flat complexes is K-flat on both sides, and all its terms are flat. This only requires the exactness and adjunction already in S.

Define each derived tensor or derived extension comparison as the inverse mate of the corresponding exact right square. Apply the normalized derived-mate representative theorem. On a common adapted resolution all counits and the ordinary comparison are invertible, so the derived comparison is invertible. Naturality and essential surjectivity of localization extend this to every derived object. The four-mates conjugation identity then makes the evaluation and restricted-direct-image mates invertible. The counit and unit mate identities give every required normalization.

Prove the ordinary inverse-transition square for every n ≤ m by induction from the successor equation in S and the normalized identity/composition equations of the strict transitions. Localization faithfulness, the evaluation representative equations, restriction naturality and the transition representative formulas prove the derived inverse-transition square. Taking mates commutes with whiskering and composition, and therefore gives the direct-transition square. Assemble the evaluation and scalar comparison records.
